notes.hist:thm:matrix_carmichael_mahler: \par\noindent\textbf{Editorial hypothesis correction.} The original displayed statement leaves the vectors untyped. Its integrality conclusion requires $v_0,w\in\Z_p^d$, $L\ge1$, and $H,j,n\in\N$ with $H>0$; the value at $Hx+j$ for $x\in\Z_p$ means the matrix-binomial interpolation. With $p=3$, $C=4$, $L=1$, $w=1$ and $v_0=1/3$, one has $\Delta_1a_0=1$, which is not in $3\Z_3$. The printed claim without these restrictions is therefore not an as-written certificate. The full original proof follows under the corrected hypotheses.\par\medskip
notes.hist:thm:finite_adelic_transfer: \par\noindent\textbf{Editorial hypothesis correction.} Read this statement with $v_0,w\in\Z^d$, $H>0$ and $j,n,r\in\N$, and positive integer $L_p$. These restrictions make the integral congruences and powers well typed. Allowing $v_0=1/3$ in the one-prime example above loses the advertised digit; invertibility of $C$ alone does not restore it. The original proof is retained under these hypotheses.\par\medskip
notes.hist:lem:matrix_power_amplification: \par\noindent\textbf{Editorial hypothesis correction.} Require $L\ge1$. At $L=0$ the standalone claim is false: for $p=3$, $d=1$ and $X=2=1+B$, one has $X^3-1=7\notin3\Z_3$. With $L\ge1$, every higher binomial term in the retained proof has the required valuation, including $p=2$.\par\medskip
notes.hist:thm:matrix_polyphase_precision: \par\noindent\textbf{Editorial hypothesis correction.} Require $L\ge1$, $C,B\in M_d(\Z_p)$, $v_0,w\in\Z_p^d$, $H>0$, and $a,j,n,r\in\N$. These are the hypotheses of the two corrected matrix statements used by the retained proof. Without integral observation vectors or positive $L$, the preceding counterexamples invalidate the claimed precision.\par\medskip
notes.hist:thm:prime_power_sparsification: \par\noindent\textbf{Editorial hypothesis correction.} The affine-kernel congruence below needs no change, but its consequence for transformed Mahler coefficients requires $c_r\in\Z_p$ for every $r$. Convergence of a $\Q_p$-valued Mahler expansion alone is insufficient. For $p=2$, $M=2$, $s=0$ and $f(x)=x/2$, one has $c_1=1/2$, $c_2=0$, while $g(q)=q$ has $d_1=1$; thus $d_1\not\equiv c_2\pmod2$. The coefficient consequence is read with integral original coefficients.\par\medskip
notes.hist:ex:compressed_mod_seven: \par\noindent\textbf{Editorial numerical correction.} The positive-index standard-window tail printed below is erroneous. The defining recurrence gives $e_1=-1\equiv6$, $e_2=5$ and $e_3=-61\equiv2\pmod7$, so the correct positive tail is $6,5,2,6,5,2,\ldots$. The period-three conclusion remains correct. The original line is retained only as a corrected historical record.\par\medskip
notes.hist:cor:local_source_change: \par\noindent\textbf{Editorial range correction.} This comparison holds for the even source subsequences, equivalently the evenized generating functions $H_p$. It does not identify their full odd-degree source values. For $p=3$, the original odd source has $A_{3,1}=S_1(3)=3$, whereas every odd dyadic source coefficient is zero; the even kernel $L_3K_2$ cannot change that odd coefficient. Read the coefficient consequence below only at even indices. The displayed identity $H_p=L_pK_\ell H_\ell$ and its proof remain valid.\par\medskip
notes.hist:thm:exact_dyadic_kernel_weight: \par\noindent\textbf{Editorial index conventions.} The standalone kernel valuation holds for all $r\ge1$. Its reconstruction-term formula requires even $n\ge0$ and $1\le r\le n/2$. In the following truncation formulas only terms with $r\le n/2$ occur; terms that would use $R_{n-2r}$ at a negative index are omitted. An empty tail is exactly zero, and the minimum over an empty set of term valuations is $+\infty$. These conventions include $M\ge n/2$.\par\medskip
